Viñas Urquiza, que intenta señalar un acento primario y otro secundario, termina por reconocer (1, 48) que «por razones de ritmo» el acento varía de posición. ... La misma palabra se ve que puede recibir el acento en distintas sílabas: 9, 1, Tagfwái/9, 7, Tágfwaj.' NERCESIAN 2011:81: 'Stress in Wichí is rhythmic, derived by parsing the word into binary iambic feet from left to right. The language has a quantity-insensitive stress system; syllable weight does not influence stress placement. The primary stress is applied to the head of the rightmost foot in the phonological word. audit.recode_to: QI-FIXED final (iambs L->R, primary on head of rightmost foot = word-final; weight-insensitive by explicit statement; domain WORD; exceptions listed-set: extrametrical Type I locative/directional suffixes -> penult, noun-incorporation root-stress template; rule_string '01 001 0001...' as already drafted in the adjudicator's notes), with Tovar 1981's phrase-rhythm account demoted to a caution note; evidence grade upgradable to publisher-text (Nercesian 2014 LINCOM / UBA thesis PDF).
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding quotations (Tovar 1981:172; Nercesian 2011:81, 97) and the Terraza 2009:53-54 support are verbatim at the stated places in the held files. (2) Deciding source: the typed fields rest on Nercesian 2011 (Amerindia), a metrical analysis with acoustic checking that is the article form of Glottolog's MED grammar; the CONFLICT verdict exists only because Tovar 1981 (impressionistic accent marks in a text collection, Vejoz-proper informant) denies word stress. (3) fetched sources now: the MED itself (Nercesian 2011 thesis, sec. 4.2.1 p. 171) and Nercesian 2014 LINCOM (pp. 121-122) confirm the rule verbatim; Terraza & Cayré Baito 2014 (Rivadavia Banda Sur, Salta + Ing. Juárez) independently state word-level, quantity-insensitive, final primary stress unaffected by suffixes/enclitics; Hunt 1913 (Vejoz proper, p. 39) already treats accent as word-level with disyllables mostly

sources.citation: Nercesian, Verónica. 2011. Gramática del wichí, una lengua chaqueña: Interacción fonología-morfología-sintaxis en el léxico. Tesis doctoral, Universidad de Buenos Aires (2 vols; repositorio.filo.uba.ar handle filodigital/1466). Glottolog MED for wich1263.
sources.quote: 'El wichí organiza las sílabas de la palabra fonológica en pies yámbicos binarios de izquierda a derecha. La lengua es insensible al peso por tanto sílabas CV y CVC son consideradas indistintamente como sílabas livianas para la asignación del acento. Éste sigue un patrón rítmico, se aplica al núcleo del pie más a la derecha de la palabra fonológica. ... No existen palabras básicas con más de tres sílabas.' Sec. 2.5: the vernacular 'arribeños del Bermejo' group comprises Embarcación, Misión Chaqueña, Rivadavia Banda Sur (i.e. Tovar's Vejoz area); the thesis describes the 'abajeños del Bermejo'
sources.locator: vol. 1, sec. 4.2.1 'División en pies métricos y asignación de acento', printed p. 171 (PDF p. 173); dialect scope sec. 2.5 pp. 55-56

sources.citation: Hunt, Richard J. 1913. El Vejoz ó Aiyo. Revista del Museo de La Plata 22 (segunda serie, t. 9): 7-215 (archive.org item elvejozaiyo00hunt, scanned text).
sources.quote: 'Por lo general la voz carga sobre la radical del sentido: las voces simples de dos sílabas, como ha-lá, las más de las veces son agudas, es decir, acentúan la final.' A word-level, final-tending statement for Vejoz proper (aiyo), the same sub-variety as Tovar's informant.
sources.locator: Gramática (author's part), cap. II 'El acento', p. 39 (scanned lines 2459-2463; índice line 25326)
sources.note: Earliest Vejoz-proper grammar; cap. II p. 39 treats accent as word-level with disyllables mostly oxytone, a second Vejoz-proper witness against Tovar's phrase-only reading.

sources.quote: 'El wichí organiza las sílabas de la palabra fonológica en pies yámbicos binarios de izquierda a derecha. La lengua es insensible al peso, por lo tanto sílabas CV y CVC son consideradas indistintamente para la asignación del acento. Éste sigue un patrón rítmico, se aplica al núcleo del pie más a la derecha de la palabra fonológica.' Same examples ten.té, ʔi.nót, ʔa.tsì.n̥á, ʔis.tì.wín.
sources.note: Published version of the MED; sec. 4.2.1 pp. 121-122 restates the rule; lets evidence grade move from scanned/open-text to publisher text.

sources.citation: Terraza, Jimena & Lorena Cayré Baito. 2014. Phonological, grammatical, and written words in Wichi. Morphology 24(3). DOI 10.1007/s11525-014-9240-1 (author offprint on CONICET Digital, hdl 11336/8887). Data: Rivadavia Banda Sur (Salta) and Ingeniero Juárez (Formosa).
sources.quote: 'The stress pattern of Wichí is quantity-insensitive; that is, primary stress falls on the rightmost syllable of the word regardless of syllable weight (Cayré Baito 2013)' ... 'the stress pattern is not modified by the suffixes or enclitics that are added to the stem. Moreover, none of the prefixes affect the stress pattern and they are themselves always unstressed' ... 3.2.1 'there is one primary stress per word assigned to the rightmost syllable'. Fn. 9: 'stress in Wichí requires a thorough study, since it does not always appear to be regular ... some suffixes present a double behavior'. Ter
sources.locator: sec. 3.2 'Stress' and 3.2.1, offprint PDF p. 14-15; fn. 9
sources.note: Only modern statement for a Salta/Bermejo-arribeño variety (Rivadavia Banda Sur) near Tovar's Vejoz: word-level, quantity-insensitive, final primary stress; weakens the Tovar phrase-only leg of the CONFLICT.
